data.name: Horia
data.gender_notes: Horia is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Hurriya' which means 'freedom' or 'liberation'. In Islamic tradition, it is also associated with the concept of 'Noor' or 'Light' which represents the divine guidance and enlightenment. The name Horia carries the meaning “Light, Radiance” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Horia usually hope their child will grow to embody light, radiance and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner light and guidance from Allah.
data.etymology: Horia belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Light, Radiance.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Horia total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: حورية

in_urdu.name: حوریہ
in_urdu.meaning: حوریہ کا مطلب ہے آزادی اور نئی تخلیق

in_hindi.name: हुरिया
in_hindi.meaning: हुरिया का अर्थ है स्वतंत्रता और नई रचना
in_hindi.long_meaning: हुरिया एक अरबी मूल का स्त्रीलिंग नाम है, जो 'हूर' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है बेहतर की ओर परिवर्तन। इस्लामी परंपरा में, यह नाम गुलामी और पापों से मुक्ति, और सुंदरता और पवित्रता से विशिष्ट एक नई रचना से जुड़ा है। कुरआन में 'हूर' का उल्लेख जन्नत और बहिश्त के संदर्भ में किया गया है, जहां हूर को फखार की तरह स्लेट से बनाए जाने का वर्णन किया गया है

in_english.name: Horia
in_english.meaning: Freedom and new creation in Islamic context
in_english.long_meaning: Horia is a feminine given name of Arabic origin, derived from 'hūr', meaning change or transformation towards better. In Islamic tradition, the name is associated with freedom from slavery and sins, and a new creation characterized by beauty and purity. The term 'hūr' is mentioned in the Quran in the context of paradise and gardens, describing them as created from clay like pottery. The name symbolizes liberation, renewal, and spiritual growth, reflecting values of compassion, peace, and divine grace

Hence, Horia is a reminder of the importance of inner enlightenment and seeking knowledge, as essential components of faith. This dual meaning – the outer reality of freedom and the inner reality of illumination – makes the name Horia a powerful embodiment of the interconnectedness between spiritual growth and individual empowerment.
